items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And Geechee Robinson, you once told me about, you were with Fletcher Henderson for a while. [INTERVIEWEE] After he left my band. Yeah.

ctx.x: But he's one of the first clarinetists that would play like, oh, Buster Biel and Noah and fellas like that. And there was a clarinetist, I'm trying to think of his name, in Dallas. He left and went to Europe.

When you once told me there was a Buster Biel in Texas, it was not the same guy that was with Henderson. No, it was different. That may be the same name. I just wondered if he used strange harmonies or Buster Smith, you know, they compare him with Charlie Parker and all that.

Well, not that type of playing, no, but he was a fantastic musician as far as tonation and knowing his instrument because he could also do good arranging. He was responsible for Con Basie's theme song, One O'Clock Jump. He wrote that and Basie went ahead and like the other people done, just went ahead and said, it's his number, but it's actually Buster Smith song. I didn't know. That's right. Well, I see in those days, Con Basie was around there with the Blue Devils. Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland Oakland…

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1961-05-11
items.q: The one you're referring to I think is the one that was with Fletcher Henderson.

ctx.x: Well I know Buster quite well.

Now there is two Buster Bailey's. The one you're referring to I think is the one that was with Fletcher Henderson. Yeah. Well there is another one that was from Dallas that went to Europe and never came back. Well I don't know. Did he play Clarence also? Yes he was terrific. Really?
I didn't know that. Two of them.
